story.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
paras: The Blackhawks (6-14-2) lost 4-2 to Columbus on Thursday, and the Flames (10-12-1) lost 4-1 to Minnesota the same night. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Flames sixth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd).

The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.318) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .393, and their goaltending has held them back. The Flames’ record (.457) is about what their chances are worth.

The Flames (32nd) and the Blackhawks (31st) both have struggled on the power play. The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest) and don’t block many shots (32nd). Chicago has scored 2.45 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 4.05, the second most. On the other side, the Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). Calgary has scored 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks, and they have the edge over the Blackhawks on physicality.

Sam Rinzel (1 G / 13 A / 14 P in 21 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Frank Nazar (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring. Matt Coronato (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind, with five goals in eight games against Chicago since 2023-24.
Drew Commesso is expected to start for Chicago, his first start of the season, and Dustin Wolf (5-6-1 / .877 SV% in 12 GS) for Calgary.
